title: Health Professionals’ Volunteering in Emergency Medical Teams and Its Association With Quality of Care
summary:
International studies show that both structured training and real deployment experience contribute significantly to the development of specific disaster and crisis competencies (Said & Chiang, 2020; Bodas et al., 2021; Kaim et al., 2025). However, there has not yet been a systematic empirical investigation into the extent to which acquired competencies can be used as a national resource.

This study addresses this research gap by analysing structural data from German EMT organisations, surveying EMT members’ subjective perceptions of their competencies, and validating these findings through a Delphi process with experts.
conditions: Scientific investigation of the contribution of German WHO-classified Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) to strengthening national disaster preparedness.
